A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiGS-based code-understanding study, renamed from BiGSCoder to CodeSSM. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLM training and validation results, four downstream benchmark evaluations, and architectural and training ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark evaluations, baseline comparisons, inference resource measurements, kernel analyses and a qualitative failure case.

M1.justification: The proposed 12-layer bidirectional gated SSM, MLM objective, tokenizer and initialization remain unchanged. Positional-embedding, dropout, DFT and unidirectional variants are retained under revised names. The omitted model-depth experiments concern configuration coverage rather than a revised computational procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds StackOverflow answer retrieval, DiverseVul vulnerability detection and seven-class Java complexity prediction. The original four tasks remain, with defect detection now identified as Devign and text-to-code search as NLCodeSearch. CodeSearchNet and StarCoder remain the pretraining corpora.

E2.justification: RoCoder and Zamba enter comparisons on retained benchmarks. Devign additionally includes GraphCodeBERT and CodeT5, while the new complexity-prediction comparison includes UniXcoder. These are reported comparison entries, whereas several corresponding models were only cited or absent in v1; CodeBERT and BertCoder remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds 256-context StarCoder pretraining comparisons, 1024-token SQA and complexity evaluations, and inference benchmarking at lengths 512, 1024 and 2048. The six- and 23-layer configuration evaluations disappear. Some original 512-context evaluations remain in Appendix H, so that configuration was not entirely removed.

E4.justification: Length-extrapolation comparisons expand, dropout robustness is examined on the small complexity benchmark, and Appendices F–G add kernel spectra and a worked type-inference failure case. Conversely, v1's model-depth scaling study and downstream failure results for the DFT variant disappear. The original MLM architectural ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark point estimates without seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The MLM plots retain shaded traces without defining a statistical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for three benchmarks, new comparators and configurations, and memory/throughput measurements, while removing model-depth result rows. StarCoder-trained 2048-context search MRR changes from 28.37 to 29.88. Its type-inference F1 is inconsistent within v3: 0.625 in Table 2 versus 0.619 in Table 11, which retains v1's value. These are reporting differences, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds a short mathematical comparison of SSM transfer functions and self-attention, including magnitude, phase and transformation assumptions in Equations 7–9. The background SSM and BiGS equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or formal proof is provided.

C1.justification: v3 adds a headline quantitative claim of approximately 64% lower inference memory at context length 2048 and gives greater prominence to outperforming transformers on longer unseen contexts. These extend the principal contribution beyond v1's sample-efficiency and code-understanding claims, which remain central.

C2.justification: v3 adds expressivity and parameterization limitations, phase-based mechanism arguments, and a single-kernel explanation for failures in complex local contexts. It also qualifies when larger datasets favor transformers. Conversely, it drops v1's large-model overfitting exception and broadens the dropout-based claim that CodeSSM does not overfit.

D1.justification: v3 supplies numerical learning-rate and weight-decay settings, dataset split counts, additional model configurations, and code/weight links where v1 only promised weights. It revises the GPU description from A180 to A100. However, v1's explicit context-dependent batch sizes, 120k-step GitHub-issues stage and BertCoder initialization details are no longer specified; CodeSSM initialization and tokenizer details are mainly relocated.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against hybrid/selective SSMs and recent work on state tracking, token selection and SSM parameterization. New discussion includes Zamba2, Mamba, Merrill and colleagues, Nishikawa and Suzuki, and spectral state-space models, extending beyond v1's emphasis on attention efficiency and convolutional alternatives.

P1.justification: The title and model terminology change throughout, and the introduction and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The combined results/discussion becomes separate Results and seven Research Questions sections; implementation material moves into appendices, and limitations and ethical considerations receive separate sections.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the architecture diagram, adds an efficiency overview and kernel-spectrum figures, and consolidates several benchmark tables. Detailed clone and type-inference metrics move to Appendix H, and the appendices change from single-column to two-column layout. Existing MLM plots and many table entries are redisplayed rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important evidential gaps through a RoPE baseline, 256-to-1024-context SQA evaluation, and direct memory/throughput measurements, strengthening support for its central extrapolation and efficiency claims. Failure analysis and concrete reproducibility information add further value. Conflicting type-inference values in Tables 2 and 11 and Appendix F's unjustified claim that transformers cannot forget information are material weaknesses, but the empirical and reproducibility gains still constitute a substantial net improvement.
